draft.summary: Nepal's food delivery market is a nascent but growing segment within the global online food delivery industry, which was valued at approximately $156.75–$288.8 billion in 2024 depending on the source and is projected to grow at a CAGR of roughly 9–12% through the early 2030s [F1, F3, F4]. The Nepali market is concentrated in Kathmandu and a handful of secondary cities, with Foodmandu (founded 2010, Series B funded) and Pathao Food as the established incumbents, and newer entrants like Yango increasing competition [F7, F8, F9, F10]. Several smaller, unfunded startups such as BhojMandu, Foodganj, and WL Food also operate in Kathmandu [F6].

competitors.name: Foodmandu
competitors.note: Founded in 2010, Series B funded (investors include Team Ventures and True North Associates). Operates across Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, Pokhara, Chitwan, and Butwal, claiming the widest restaurant range and delivery hours from 7 AM to 12 AM.

competitors.name: Pathao Food
competitors.note: Leverages its existing ride-hailing user base to offer food delivery in Kathmandu. Considered an established incumbent alongside Foodmandu, and now faces direct competition from Yango's market entry.

observations: The global online food delivery market is projected to reach $505.5 billion by 2030 (CAGR ~9.4%) or $667.04 billion by 2032 (CAGR ~11.92%), depending on the research source, but none of these reports provide Nepal-specific market size data [F1, F4].
Nepal's food delivery ecosystem is dominated by two incumbents—Foodmandu and Pathao Food—with Yango recently entering the market and intensifying competition [F7, F8, F9].
Multiple small, unfunded startups (BhojMandu, Foodganj, WL Food, Opasa) launched in 2020–2021 in Kathmandu, suggesting low barriers to entry but also difficulty in securing funding [F6].

Kathmandu-specific operational challenges include kitchen capacity vs. courier supply mismatch, narrow alley routing for deliveries, and cash-on-delivery reconciliation across 100+ restaurants daily [F8].

Building an MVP food delivery app for the Nepal market is estimated at 8–14 months and NPR 40–120 lakh; new entrants are advised to find a specific niche (cuisine, geography, or corporate) to compete [F8].
Foodmandu is the most established player, founded in 2010 with Series B funding from Team Ventures and True North Associates, and operates in five cities across Nepal [F7, F10].
